Subject: Capacity planning for NovaWorks: Q4 latency & region asks

Hi Lukas,

Thanks for taking the initial inbound — quick summary of where we are: NovaWorks is preparing to launch an AI-assisted search experience across North America, EU and APAC in Q4. We're forecasting a 3x traffic ramp (concurrent sessions + async batch jobs) from November through January. Critical asks:

- Latency SLOs: 95th <= 220ms for NA/EU, <= 180ms for APAC (initial pilot in Singapore/HK).
- Preferred setup: dedicated inference capacity (we need regionally isolated pools for data residency and latency).
- Expected monthly token volume: ~1.8B tokens/month in peak (split roughly 50% US, 30% EU, 20% APAC).
- Procurement timeline: target to sign reserved capacity SOW by 2026-11-15.

Can you share an initial approach to sizing / SKU mix (we're flexible on model variants but want predictable unit economics) and a suggested mutual action plan? Attaching a small traffic projection to help.

Attachments: nova_traffic_projection_oct2026.csv (traffic by region & hour)

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-minute call if that's easier.

Elena Park
Head of Platform Engineering
NovaWorks
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@novaworks.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity planning for NovaWorks: Q4 latency & region asks

Elena — appreciate the clear brief and the projection. High-level response below; Ben and Ops (Irene) are looped in to validate technical sizing and run feasibility for the timelines you mentioned.

Summary approach (short):
- Latency-led SKU allocation: prioritize smaller, lower-queue GPU lanes in APAC to hit 95th <= 180ms, accept slightly higher unit cost. For US/EU, balance throughput-first SKUs with modest batching to reduce unit cost while staying under 220ms.
- Preliminary sizing (very rough):
  - US: equivalent of 6 x A100-80GB-class nodes (sustained) + 2 burst nodes for traffic spikes
  - EU: equivalent of 4 x A100-80GB-class nodes (sustained) + 1 burst node
  - APAC: equivalent of 3 x A100-80GB-class nodes (low-queue config) + 1 burst node
- Model assumptions: baseline model family is L3-32b quantized (we can swap to a cheaper 13B if you want to optimize cost).
- Next steps: 1) Ben to run token/hour -> GPU-hour translation and checklist for region provisioning; 2) Ops (Irene) to confirm compliance paths for EU data residency; 3) Lauren to kick procurement conversation/term questions and send a mutual action plan template.

I'm available for a call tomorrow afternoon PST. Proposed slots: Tue 05 Oct 16:00-17:00 UTC or Wed 06 Oct 01:00-02:00 UTC.

Lukas
Product Sales Engineer — Redwood Inference

Folks — I pulled the projection and did a quick run using our L3-32B throughput profile. Notes below and attached initial sizing sheet.

Key assumptions (for transparency):
- Model: L3-32B quant (one KV cache per session), 1.8B tokens/month peak (Elena's split).
- Effective tokens/sec at 95th given our batching strategy: US/EU ~ 130 t/s per A100-80 equiv; APAC ~ 90 t/s per A100-80 equiv (keeping queue depth minimal).

Preliminary sizing (sustained equivalent):
- US: ~5.8 A100-80 equiv -> round to 6 nodes (adds capacity headroom + planned backups)
- EU: ~3.6 A100-80 equiv -> round to 4 nodes
- APAC: ~2.9 A100-80 equiv -> round to 3 nodes, but configure with low-batch lanes and higher freq pre-warming to meet 95th latency 

Operational asks / risks:
- APAC availability: lead time for compliant SG/HK node activation is ~4–6 weeks depending on capacity sourcing; if procurement must be complete by 2026-11-15 we should start procurement conversation this week.
- Fallback policy: recommend a cross-region soft-fail to EU for non-PII traffic; requires consent and routing rules in mutual action plan.
- Cost estimate (baseline, monthly committed): approx $XXk (placeholder) — I'll finalize after we pick model variant and quantization level.

Attachments: nw_initial_sizing_v1.xlsx, latency_tradeoffs_v2.pdf

I'll prepare a short slide with the SKU mix + ops gating items by EOD Tues.

Ben
